children: Technology behemoth Apple Inc. (AAPL, Financials) is beginning the John Ternus era with a far higher bar than Tim Cook had to clear when he inherited the reins in 2011. Apple's market value has soared to over $4.6 trillion from under $350 billion when Cook assumed the CEO role.

The stock currently trades at over 33 times anticipated earnings, far above its 10-year average of about 23 times and the about 12 times multiple Apple had when Cook took over. Valuation is among Ternus' major concerns.
Cook helped expand Apple into a wider earnings machine. Revenue increased from $157 billion in fiscal 2012 to $416 billion in fiscal 2025, with Services contributing over $109 billion.
Apple has also repurchased about $840 billion in shares since fiscal 2012, lowering its share count by approximately 45%.
Now Ternus needs to maintain that financial discipline while also investing more aggressively in artificial intelligence, research and development and perhaps larger acquisitions.
Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan said Apple's move away from a net-cash-neutral target could indicate more spending on R&D, capital expenditures and M&A.

Apple is set to announce new products on Sept. 9 so the next test is just around the corner. Investors will want to see if Ternus can deliver enough fresh growth to justify a valuation substantially larger than the one Cook inherited.

title: Apple's New CEO Inherits a 33x Valuation and an $840 Billion Legacy
